product_one_liner.value: Fly.io provides hardware-isolated cloud virtual machines, agent sandboxes and managed PostgreSQL for developers and engineering teams deploying applications and AI agents.

hq_location.notes: PitchBook identifies San Francisco as headquarters; the company’s legal contact address is there. LinkedIn and Y Combinator instead list Chicago.

eng_blog.notes: Technical posts explain Phoenix LiveView implementation and Fly’s orchestrator/scheduler architecture.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: The public jobs index lists Platform Security Engineer, Fullstack Engineer, Infrastructure Operations Engineer and Networking Engineer; none has a qualifying AI/ML/data-science title.

model_provider.notes: Disclosed uses are internal platform tooling: AI-assisted log analysis, support responses and signup classification (Anthropic), and incident summaries (OpenAI), not a customer-facing hosted foundation model. OpenRouter is also listed, but its notice says processing does not begin before 2026-11-23, after the requested cutoff.

compliance_certs.notes: SOC 2 Type 2 is claimed. ISO 27001 refers to datacenter operators, not Fly.io; HIPAA BAAs and GDPR DPAs are contractual compliance offerings, not certifications. Fly.io says it does not hold ISO 27001 or a PCI DSS AOC.

raised_18mo.notes: The $25 million Series D was announced July 24, 2026, within 2025-05-09 through 2026-11-09.

hiring_sdr_ae.notes: The public jobs index lists four engineering roles and no qualifying SDR, BDR or account executive role.

launched_6mo.notes: The changelog announces Managed Postgres v2 forking beta on 2026-07-16 and the new Fly MCP beta on 2026-10-23, within the requested six-month window.

leadership_change_12mo.notes: On July 24, 2026, Fly.io announced Scott Johnston had joined as CEO and founder Kurt Mackey would transition to an advisory role while remaining on the board.

crm_stack_signal.notes: The subprocessor list identifies HubSpot and Snowflake for customer relationship management, Customer.io for newsletters and transactional email, and Mailgun for transactional email.
